text:
alex: noticing a sudden tail-latency spike from SFO1 p3/dedicated pools ~10m ago. 99p ~3.1s for short prompts, baseline ~0.9s. queue depth trending up. opening triage now.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-SFO-LAT (auto) — severity: high — bridge: #inc-bridge-2179993456

tanya: thanks alex. are metrics pointing to GPU stalls or network egress? can you paste the kernel error logs?

alex: looks like kernel scheduling stalls on ~7 nodes. metrics: GPU_UTIL steady, but SM stalls and power capping events. logs: ```[kernel] stall_detected: 0x3f at 14:02:11
nvml: Throttle: PowerCapTriggered```

michael: copying graphs into bridge. I'm seeing increased packet retransmits on the NVMe network on nodes that report stalls. hypothesis: firmware/driver regression after yesterday's kernel module bump.

sophia: if it's driver regression we should isolate p3 pools and shift traffic. proposal: enable traffic-slice for SFO1 and route new requests to us-central2/eur1 read replicas while we remediate. costs: cross-region egress + burst capacity. ok with that?

alex: agree. executing controlled traffic-slice now: slice=0.6 -> keep 60% in SFO1 for critical customers, 40% routed out. will monitor queue depth.

support-oncall: prepping customer comms. draft status page blurb: "We are investigating increased inference latency in SFO1 affecting some dedicated GPU pools. We are routing a portion of traffic to alternate regions; some customers may see elevated latency or cost while we remediate. ETA 2 hours for initial mitigation." feedback?

tanya: tweak: include guidance for customers on pinned capacity — "If you have pinned SFO1-only Dedicated capacity, you may see degraded latency until we complete the kernel rollback or node restart. Contact support for opt-in relocation."

michael: rolling kernel-module rollback on a single hit group now (nd-07). will observe for 5min before wider rollout. command: ```ansible-playbook rollback-driver.yml -l nd-07 --extra-vars "module_version=nv-driver-2.3.1"```

ops-bot: Bridge #inc-bridge-2179993456 created by alex. Participants: alex, tanya, michael, sophia, support-oncall

alex: nd-07 node group shows normalized tail latency after rollback on first batch. 99p down to 1.0s. moving to batch 2 (nd-03, nd-04).

sophia: starting update to status page: "Mitigation in progress: traffic reroute + targeted driver rollback. Impact: degraded latency for some SFO1 workloads. ETA for broad mitigation: ~90 minutes. We will update in 30 minutes or sooner."

support-oncall: posted to status.redwood.ai incident SFO-LAT-2179993456. Slack support message to customers with pinned SFO capacity sent to active contacts.

tanya: note for oncall: if rollback doesn't hold we escalate to full pool drain + live migration; cost implication estimate: ~$8k/hr while cross-region burst is active. tag finance if we exceed daily burn threshold.

michael: batch 2 completed. two nodes failed auto-restart post-rollback; manual reprovision in progress (reimage + driver install). queue depth dropping but still above baseline.

alex: manual reprovisioning ETA ~45m for the two nodes. holding 60% local slice until we hit steady state.

sophia: updating customer comms: add short-howto for customers to reduce shard size or enable model-variant fallback to smaller quantized variant to reduce tokens and latency.

support-oncall: received 3 escalations from enterprise customers; routing to eng-sre & AMs. I've flagged customers with pinned SFO-only capacity as "priority" for manual relocation.

michael: reprovision complete on the two nodes, post-reboot health checks passing. 99p now ~0.95s. monitoring for 10m then we'll declare mitigation.

alex: confirming stabilization. reducing cross-region reroute from 40% to 15% to absorb any residual load while we finish health checks.

sophia: posting final status update in 10m with root-cause hypothesis: driver/kernel regression triggered power-capping behavior on select GPU SKUs, causing SM stalls. will open follow-up incident for driver rollout gating.

support-oncall: final status page update posted: "Mitigation complete — service stabilized in SFO1. Residual routing remains while we validate. Postmortem and customer-facing RCA will follow within 72 hours. If you need immediate assistance, reply to your support thread." :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-SFO-LAT resolved by alex. Duration: ~1h2m. Postmortem assigned to michael and tanya (due in 72h).

alex: nice work team. tag: postmortem owners will add timeline, impact matrix, and follow-up to rollout gating for driver updates.

support-oncall: closing bridge. customers notified individually where needed.
